#   `factory` holds a known-good golden image. ESP-IDF's OTA rotation never
#   targets a factory partition
so it cannot be overwritten by an update.

# DBB Companion - ESP32-S3-WROOM-1 N16R8: #   The bootloader falls back to it in two independent ways:
#     1. both otadata entries invalid -> "Defaulting to factory image"
#     2. the selected app image fails to verify -> the backwards partition
#        scan terminates at factory
#   `app_count` counts only ota_* partitions
so it is 2 here. The bootloader's

# DBB Companion - ESP32-S3-WROOM-1 N16R8: #   (ota_seq - 1) % app_count therefore matches the firmware's two-slot
#   rotation exactly. Adding a third ota_* slot would break that agreement.
# NOT A SECURE LAYOUT
#   Secure Boot and Flash Encryption are off. There are deliberately no
#   `encrypted` flags and no nvs_keys partition: NVS encryption requires flash
#   encryption
#   that would involve a serial reflash anyway. Reserving space for it buys
#   nothing. Do not reintroduce either without a deliberate decision.
# DEVELOPMENT ARTIFACT
#   This table serves development. The final one gets built when the product is
#   ready and the target silicon is chosen - the ESP32-S3 may not be the part a
#   year from now. Do not optimise it for hypothetical future needs; reflashing
#   is cheap while the boards are on the desk.
# *** BEFORE RESIZING ANYTHING HERE
#   db_a and db_b are reserved for a companion data store. This base does not
#   use them
but they are load-bearing and must not be resized or removed:

# DBB Companion - ESP32-S3-WROOM-1 N16R8: #   the layout has to stay byte-identical across builds
#   images with different partition tables is not possible. The store that
#   does use them requires BOTH to be exactly 128 KiB and fails to mount -
#   silently
#   The `diag` partition is likewise read in 4096-byte records by
#   main/db_diag.c (DB_DIAG_SECTOR_SIZE); its size must stay a multiple of that
#   and at least two sectors.
#   Any resize is a full serial reflash of both boards - OTA cannot repartition.
# SIZING NOTES (revised 09-08-2026)
#   db_a/db_b were 512 KiB each. The database is capped at 768 records x 96 B =
#   72 KiB
so one 128 KiB slot per side holds every record that can ever exist.

# DBB Companion - ESP32-S3-WROOM-1 N16R8: #   A/B alternation is unchanged: consecutive generations still land in
#   different partitions
so one partition can be destroyed without loss.
